answer: The timeline preserves each saved filing, order, announcement or other event at its own recorded date. It is a historical record set, not a claim that every earlier proposal or application has the same status today.

items.title: Executive Order: Independent Agencies Answer to the White House — Except Fed Monetary Policy
kv: The order pulling independent agencies under White House review carves out the Fed's conduct of monetary policy but keeps its supervision and regulation of banks inside the fence. The seam is drawn deliberately: the money lever stays nominally independent, the bank-oversight lever does not.

items.title: Request for Information and Comment on Reserve Bank Payment Account Prototype
kv: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (Board) seeks public input on a special purpose Reserve Bank account prototype (a Payment Account) tailored to the risks and needs of institutions focused on payments innovation. A Payment Account holder would be expected to use its account for the express purpose of clearing and settling the institution's payment activity. Payment Accounts would be designed to pose limited risk to the Federal Reserve Banks (Reserve Banks) and the overall payment system, and Reserve Banks would generally conduct a streamlined review of requests for these accounts. Any institution that is legally eligible for Federal Reserve accounts or services (accounts and services) under the Federal Reserve Act would be eligible to request a Payment Account from a Reserve Bank. The Payment Account protype does not seek to expand or otherwise change legal eligibility for access to accounts and services.

items.title: Prohibition on Use of Reputation Risk or Other Supervisory Tools To Encourage or Compel Banking Organizations To Engage in Politicized or Unlawful Discrimination
kv: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (Board) is inviting public comment on a notice of proposed rulemaking (proposal or proposed rule) that would codify the removal of reputation risk from the Board's supervisory programs. The proposal would prohibit the Board from encouraging or compelling Board-supervised banking organizations to deny or condition the provision of banking or other financial products or services to an individual or business based on their constitutionally protected political or religious beliefs, associations, speech, or conduct, or based on involvement by the individual or business in politically disfavored but lawful business activities perceived to present reputation risk.

items.title: Prohibition on the Use of Reputation Risk by Regulators
kv: Treasury Department — Comptroller of the Currency

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation are adopting a final rule to codify the elimination of reputation risk from their supervisory programs. Among other things, the rule prohibits the agencies from criticizing or taking adverse action against an institution on the basis of reputation risk. The rule also prohibits the agencies from requiring, instructing, or encouraging an institution to close an account, to refrain from providing an account, product, or service, or to modify or terminate any product or service on the basis of a person or entity's political, social, cultural, or religious views or beliefs, constitutionally protected speech, or solely on the basis of politically disfavored but lawful business activities perceived to present reputation risk. The rule further forbids the agencies from taking any supervisory action or other adverse action against an institution, a group of institutions, or the institution-affiliated parties of any institution that is designed to punish or discourage an individual or group from engaging in any lawful political, social, cultural, or religious activities, constitutionally protected speech, or, for political reasons, lawful business activities that the agencies or its personnel disagree with or disfavor.

items.title: KC Fed Frames Kraken Account as Payment-Account Pilot
kv: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City

The Kansas City Fed published a supplemental document framing the Kraken Financial limited-purpose account (granted March 4, 2026) as a pilot of the Reserve Bank payment-account concept — the first live test of the prototype the Board proposed in FR 2026-10375. Only overdraft-rejecting services (Fedwire Funds) are available; neither the Kraken exchange nor other Payward subsidiaries get access. The pilot generates real-world data for the payment-account rulebook whose comment period closes July 27, 2026.

items.title: Regulation D — Master Accounts vs. Special-Purpose Payment Accounts
kv: Amends Regulation D to carve out a new category of “Payment Accounts” distinct from full master accounts, and to deny them interest on balances held at the Fed. Commenters warned that widely adopted dollar stablecoins could displace non-interest currency and erode the Fed's low-cost funding base — the central bank protecting its seat as the stablecoin era arrives.

items.title: Regulation A — No Discount-Window Access for Payment Accounts
kv: Amends Regulation A to specify that holders of the new special-purpose Payment Accounts would NOT be eligible for discount-window credit. Combined with prefunding and no-overdraft rules, this fences the new entrants off from the Fed's lender-of-last-resort backstop — onto the rails, but without the safety net.

items.title: Proposed Revisions to the Policy on Payment System Risk and the Account Access Guidelines
kv: The Board proposes a new Part IV of the Payment System Risk policy to create special-purpose “Payment Accounts” at the Reserve Banks, and revises the guidelines for who may access Reserve Bank accounts and services. Critically, it encourages Reserve Banks to PAUSE decisions on account requests from Tier 3 (riskiest, novel-charter) institutions until the policy is finished — the master-account gate, written into policy.

items.title: The Community Banks Ask Kansas City to Take Kraken's Account Back
kv: ICBA formally asks the Kansas City Fed to review immediately whether Kraken Financial's limited-purpose account squares with the account-access guidelines — and to weigh additional limits, suspension, non-renewal, or termination. Its evidence: ICIJ reporting that Kraken moved at least $1.1B in Bitcoin to crypto-ATM operators. The account runs on a one-year term; the letter builds the public record for the first renewal (~March 2027). The first organized push to close the one door a district opened.
Kraken, master account, gate, ICBA, Kansas City Fed

items.title: NCUA Final Rule: Prohibition on the Use of Reputation Risk
kv: First agency to write the debanking ban into regulation: examiners may no longer use 'reputation risk' to lean on institutions, implementing EO 14331 (Guaranteeing Fair Banking). The agency stopped examining for it in September 2025; this makes the removal permanent — the anti-debanking agenda hardening from policy into law.

items.title: Federal Reserve AML/CFT Program Proposed Rule (Docket R-1835)
kv: Board of Governors, Federal Reserve System

Comments due Sep 8, 2026. Doc 2026-13919. This was the Fed's AML rewrite flagged in the 07-08 sweep — now formally published.

fields: ICBA formally asks the Kansas City Fed to review immediately whether Kraken Financial's limited-purpose account squares with the account-access guidelines — and to weigh additional limits, suspension, non-renewal, or termination. Its evidence: ICIJ reporting that Kraken moved at least $1.1B in Bitcoin to crypto-ATM operators. The account runs on a one-year term; the letter builds the public record for the first renewal (~March 2027). The first organized push to close the one door a district opened.
Kraken, master account, gate, ICBA, Kansas City Fed

record.title: NCUA Final Rule: Prohibition on the Use of Reputation Risk
fields: First agency to write the debanking ban into regulation: examiners may no longer use 'reputation risk' to lean on institutions, implementing EO 14331 (Guaranteeing Fair Banking). The agency stopped examining for it in September 2025; this makes the removal permanent — the anti-debanking agenda hardening from policy into law.
reputation risk, debanking, NCUA, EO 14331, fair banking

record.title: Federal Reserve AML/CFT Program Proposed Rule (Docket R-1835)
fields: Board of Governors, Federal Reserve System

Proposed rule requiring Fed-supervised banks to establish risk-based AML/CFT programs, aligned with FinCEN's AML Act of 2020 implementation and parallel OCC/FDIC/NCUA changes. Comments due Sep 8, 2026. Doc 2026-13919. This was the Fed's AML rewrite flagged in the 07-08 sweep — now formally published.
AML, CFT, Federal Reserve, proposed rule, Bank Secrecy Act

record.title: Kraken Financial's CEO Testifies to Wyoming's Blockchain Committee About Its Fed Account
fields: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City

Kraken Financial CEO Brian Mathena testified to Wyoming's Select Committee on Blockchain, Financial Technology and Digital Innovation at its July 14-15, 2026 meeting; the official minutes record that he highlighted receipt of a Federal Reserve master account.
Kraken, master account, Tier 3, Kansas City Fed, Bowman, Dart Bank, Wyoming

catalog_context.title: Who actually controls the crypto infrastructure
catalog_context.answer: Of 20 crypto networks and companies we track, only one is used at scale and none is proven under stress; many brands rest on a handful of legal providers.
